stem: According to the World Health Organisation (WHO), reproductive health means
options: normal structure and working of the reproductive organs only
total well-being in physical, emotional, behavioural and social aspects
the ability of every married couple to have as many children as desired
complete freedom from sexually transmitted infections throughout life
explanation: Correct option: (B). WHO defines reproductive health as total well-being in all aspects of reproduction, i.e., physical, emotional, behavioural and social. Normal organs alone cover only the physical part; having any number of children and absence of STIs are only parts of reproductive health, not its definition.

stem: A doctor withdraws a little amniotic fluid from around a developing foetus and analyses its cells. Which use of this procedure is legally permitted in India?
options: Finding the sex of the foetus when the parents request it
Fixing the exact date on which fertilisation took place
Checking whether the mother has a sexually transmitted infection
Testing the foetus for genetic disorders such as Down syndrome
explanation: Correct option: (D). The procedure is amniocentesis; its fetal cells and dissolved substances are tested for genetic disorders such as Down syndrome, haemophilia and sickle-cell anaemia. Its use for sex determination is statutorily banned to check female foeticide. It does not date fertilisation, and it tests the foetus, not the mother, for disease.

stem: A health survey compares two decades in a state. Which set of findings would best indicate that reproductive health in that society has improved?
options: Lower maternal and infant mortality with more medically assisted deliveries
A faster rate of population growth and a larger share of people of fertile age
More amniocentesis tests for sex and more abortions in the second trimester
Larger average family size and greater sale of drugs that increase fertility
explanation: Correct option: (A). The chapter lists decreased maternal and infant mortality, more medically assisted deliveries, better post-natal care, smaller families and better detection and cure of STIs as indicators of improved reproductive health. Faster population growth is a problem, not an indicator; sex-determination tests and second-trimester abortions are dangerous or illegal practices; larger families run against the aim of small, healthy families.

stem: Removal of the gonads cannot be considered a contraceptive option. Which reason best supports this statement?
options: It halts gamete formation, but leaves sex hormones and sexual drive fully unaffected
It is irreversible and also stops sex hormones, so sexual drive and body suffer
It is fully reversible, but is too costly to offer in national programmes
It only blocks the transport of gametes, just as vasectomy and tubectomy do
explanation: Correct option: (B). Gonads produce both gametes and sex hormones. Removing them is permanent and also stops hormone secretion, which would affect sexual drive and secondary sexual characters, so it fails the ideal-contraceptive criteria (reversible, least side-effects, no interference with sexual drive). It does affect hormones, it is not reversible, and unlike sterilisation it removes the organs instead of only blocking gamete transport.

stem: A mother fully breast-feeds her baby after delivery and relies on lactational amenorrhoea. Which statement about this method is correct?

It works only in the first month because the uterus cannot receive an embryo then

explanation: Correct option: (D). During intense lactation following parturition, ovulation and hence the cycle do not occur; the method is reported effective only up to six months after parturition. stem: Which feature distinguishes diaphragms, cervical caps and vaults from condoms?

explanation: Correct option: (C). Diaphragms, cervical caps and vaults are rubber barriers inserted to cover the cervix and are reusable, whereas condoms are disposable. stem: A woman whose menstrual cycles are highly irregular plans to depend on periodic abstinence. Which evaluation of her plan is most sound?
options: It will be more reliable, since irregular cycles mean ovulation rarely occurs
It will be less reliable, since the fertile period cannot be predicted well
It will be equally reliable, since the fertile period is always day 10 to 17
It will be fully reliable if she also follows withdrawal on every fertile day
explanation: Correct option: (B). Periodic abstinence works only if the couple can avoid coitus when ovulation is expected; days 10-17 apply to a regular cycle. With irregular cycles the fertile period shifts, so the method, already one with high failure, becomes less reliable. Irregular cycles do not mean ovulation is rare, the fertile days are not fixed in such cycles, and withdrawal itself has a high failure rate, so it cannot make the method fully reliable.

stem: How does a copper-releasing IUD such as CuT help prevent pregnancy?
options: Cu ions suppress sperm motility and the fertilising capacity of sperms

It blocks the fallopian tubes so that the ovum cannot reach the uterus

explanation: Correct option: (A). IUDs increase phagocytosis of sperms in the uterus, and the Cu ions released suppress sperm motility and fertilising capacity. stem: A woman had casual unprotected intercourse about 48 hours ago and wants to avoid a possible pregnancy. Based on the chapter, which is the most suitable option?

Periodic abstinence for the remaining days of that cycle
Hormonal pills or an IUD given within 72 hours of coitus

explanation: Correct option: (C). Progestogens, progestogen-estrogen combinations or IUDs given within 72 hours of coitus are effective emergency contraceptives.
